licensed_by: kogaki#1030 -- this carrier holds the CURRENT control plane only. It is not a version ledger: superseded states, defect specimens and the history of past amendments live in git and in the issues. A change is licensed by an issue, settled by a dated owner decision where it is a decision rather than a transcription, landed here, and recorded by bumping `version` and replacing this line with the issue that licensed it. Ratification is a human act: nothing denies an edit no issue licensed, and these two fields gate no code path.

state_kinds.compute: Runs, writes no owner artifact, does not stop.
state_kinds.write: Runs a renderer bound to it and writes exactly one owner artifact. The renderer is private to the executor (write authority) and renders under the grammar_surface THIS STATE declares, never one bound to the artifact path.
state_kinds.judgment: Reaches a declared judgment point. THE EXECUTOR INVOKES THE JUDGE ITSELF (kogaki#1030): it calls the model named in this table's `judge` block, validates the returned record through this state's own refusals, and retries up to the state's `retries` before failing with the refusal text. The model is a CALLED FUNCTION and never the driver -- the executor still validates and never composes (SPEC-terrain, the typed judgment points).
state_kinds.wait: The executor stops. Nothing further runs until the owner speaks and the session re-enters (SPEC-terrain, the re-entrant executor and the wait rule).
state_kinds.terminal: The run is over. Runs nothing, writes nothing, and the executor stops without awaiting an owner. Distinct from `compute` because a generic interpreter holds no state list of its own (SPEC-terrain, the workflow table) and must read the end from the table rather than from position.

field_semantics.renders_gate_declaration: Required on every state. `true` only where the state declares a gate, and `true` is what SCHEDULES the executor's composition of that state's declaration. It NAMES THE HOOK CHAIN THAT EXECUTES THE GATE and places no obligation on a session: the executor composes the declaration and stops, the harness renders the question the declaration carries, `.claude/hooks/write-gate-capture.py` records the answer at the moment the owner gives it, and that same chain invokes the executor again. It is a statement about the table and never about the runtime asking — the post-tag-selection window's question allowlist is empty and stays empty; the executor writes a file and stops.
field_semantics.conditional: Required on every state. `false` where the state is always entered; otherwise a string naming the condition. Counted by counted_baseline.conditional_states.
field_semantics.writes: Required on every state. `null` where the state writes no owner artifact; otherwise the owner_artifacts key it writes.
field_semantics.grammar_surface: Required on every state whose `writes` is non-null, and absent otherwise. Names the report-format.json surface whose line_class allowlist governs THIS state's render. The binding is per state, never per artifact path (SPEC-terrain, write authority).
field_semantics.gate_id: Required on every state whose `renders_gate_declaration` is true, and absent otherwise. Names the src/gate-registry.json gate the state declares. A property this table exists to carry may not be read off a missing key, so the two conditions are one biconditional over the states array and NOT a count: this note deliberately enumerates no number of gate states, because the count moved from three to four at kogaki#856 and a note carrying it would have gone stale in the same commit — which is the defect kogaki#807 repaired one field over, in the `owner_reads` note that used to read "Three keys" and enumerate them.
field_semantics.retries: Required on every state whose `kind` is `judgment`, and absent otherwise. The number of times the executor RE-ASKS the judge after a response its own refusals rejected; 0 means the first refusal is final. Declared PER STATE rather than once for the table because the states differ in how much a re-ask can plausibly repair -- and declared HERE rather than in the executor because the count is a property of the workflow, which is what this carrier holds.
field_semantics.per_group: Optional on a state whose `kind` is `judgment`, and absent otherwise; absence means false. `true` makes the state ONE JUDGE CALL PER COMPOSED GROUP, each carrying that group's members alone, with the per-group records assembled into the typed per-group record the state's existing validator reads -- so no refusal moves and no validation is re-implemented (kogaki#1062). A group whose record is refused is re-asked with its own prior refusal, to this state's `retries`, without re-asking the groups that passed. Declared HERE rather than in the executor for `retries`' own reason: how much work one ask carries is a property of the workflow, and a second state joins by adding this key rather than by editing code. WHY `J2_subdivision` CARRIES IT AND `J1_claims` DOES NOT: J1 composes one sentence per group and measured ~70s over the whole input, inside the bound; J2 subdivides the same groups into SubGroups each carrying a coherence label and a sentence, which is strictly more work and straddled the bound on 2026-09-09. The per-call bound is unchanged and the work per call is what shrank.
field_semantics.judge: A table-level block, not a state field. Names the command the executor runs for every judgment state, THE MODEL IT PINS, and the output format it parses. THE MODEL IS PINNED HERE AND NEVER INHERITED FROM THE SESSION (kogaki#1030): a judgment whose model is whatever happened to be driving is not reproducible, and the run record could not say what judged it. `KOGAKI_JUDGE_CLI` overrides the resolved binary FOR FIXTURES ONLY and is how the acceptance fixtures stub the call; it changes no other behaviour and pins no model of its own. It also declares `timeout_s`, the per-CALL bound in seconds -- named apart from the advance hook's own timeout because one bounds a call and the other bounds an advance.
field_semantics.record_example: Optional on a state whose `kind` is `judgment`, and absent otherwise. The LITERAL record shape, filled from the run's own composed input and put in front of the judge beside the `input_shape` sentence -- because a prose description of a shape cannot bind a validator's shape. On 2026-09-09 the live judge returned a record that satisfied `J1_claims`'s sentence and its validator refused three times (the pin as a string rather than the pin object the subset check reads `groups` out of, and the claims as an array rather than a `{group: claim}` map), the literal shape living only in a source comment and in the refusal text -- neither of which the judge sees (kogaki#1059). Values are literals except for two directives, refused by name: `$input:<key>` is the composed input's top-level <key> verbatim, and `$per-group:<text>` is an object mapping each composed group's name to <text>. `$per-group` MAY ALSO STAND AS THE SOLE KEY OF THE EXAMPLE ITSELF, whose value is then the per-group template and may be any JSON value (kogaki#1062). That is the same directive in a second POSITION and not a third directive: `J1_claims`'s record wraps its per-group map under a `claims` key, so the string form under an ordinary key expresses it, while `J2_subdivision`'s record IS the per-group map and its entries are objects rather than sentences -- so a state whose whole record is the map had no way to bind its shape by example and stayed bound by prose, which is the very defect this field closed for its sibling. FILLED FROM THE INPUT rather than written out here, because a hand-written example is a further carrier of the shape that can drift from the validator exactly as the prose did.

judge.note: The executor invokes this for every `judgment` state: `<command> -p --model <model> --output-format <output_format>`, the state's prompt on stdin, the typed record parsed out of the response. A response the state's refusals reject is re-asked up to that state's `retries` and then the run FAILS with the refusal text -- the judgment provenance state `observed` has a producer from this act on, because the Harness now holds an invocation record its own act wrote. `effort` IS THE PIN'S FOURTH COMPONENT AND IS DECLARED RATHER THAN OBSERVED: the call carries no effort flag, so this names the tier the run declares it is asking at, exactly as the judge pin has always been a declaration. What is no longer a declaration is `model` -- it is now the model the executor actually ran, which is why the pin is worth more after kogaki#1030 than before it, not less. `timeout_s` BOUNDS ONE CALL, AND IT IS NOW DERIVED FROM MEASURED WORK RATHER THAN FROM THE BUDGET ABOVE IT (kogaki#1062). It was 90 because .claude/hooks/advance-terrain.py killed the whole advance at 480 and a span could make up to six calls; nothing in that derivation asked how long a judgment call actually takes, and on 2026-09-09 the measurement arrived and refuted it. `J1_claims` -- the SMALLER judgment, 11 claims over the whole composed input -- took about 70 seconds, already 78% of the bound; `J2_subdivision` subdivided the same 11 groups over 220 placements into SubGroups each carrying a coherence label and a coherence_why sentence, which is strictly more work, and it STRADDLED the bound: two of three attempts exceeded it. SO THE BOUND STAYS AT 90 AND THE WORK PER CALL SHRINKS. `J2_subdivision` declares `per_group`, so it is one call per composed group carrying that group's members alone -- well inside 90s -- rather than one call over all of them. Raising `timeout_s` instead would have made the arithmetic worse, not better: 6 x 90s = 540s already exceeded the 480s advance budget, so a repair that only raised the per-call bound widened that gap. AND THE ADVANCE BUDGET'S OWN RE-DERIVATION IS OWED, NOT DONE HERE, and that is stated rather than left as an omission (kogaki#1062 item 4, DEFERRED at the owner's selection 2026-09-10). `ADVANCE_TIMEOUT_S` in .claude/hooks/advance-terrain.py is UNCHANGED at 480, and 480 is NOT a measured figure -- it is the number the budget-first derivation this note has just refuted produced, kept because replacing it collides with a ratified invariant rather than because it is right. THE COLLISION, named so the next reader does not re-discover it: item 4's derivation is groups x this per-call bound + margin, which at the 11 groups the 2026-09-09 run composed is 1200, while checks/check-terrain-hook-invocation.sh asserts ADVANCE_TIMEOUT_S stays BELOW the harness's 600s hook default -- a bound at or above the default can never fire first, so the timeout relay it exists for would be unreachable (PR #1034 round 1, finding 3). The two cannot both hold, and the surface that gives way -- the harness default via the machine-local registration this repository does not commit, the per-call bound, the group ceiling, or the one-advance-per-span guarantee -- is a decision rather than an implementation choice. WHAT THIS REPAIR DOES WITHOUT IT: the per-group ask makes each call small, so the per-call bound is no longer straddled, which is the defect that stalled the run; whether eleven small calls plus J1 fit inside 480 is unmeasured, and the honest state is that nobody has measured a per-group call yet. HOW PER-GROUP RETRIES WOULD SIT INSIDE ANY SUCH PRODUCT, stated here because it binds whichever number is chosen: the worst case is groups x (retries + 1) = 33 calls, which no margin priced at one call per group covers -- that overflow is the hook timeout relaying a real fact rather than a bound hiding it, the same posture the six-call arithmetic took before it. What the per-call bound guarantees is that a HUNG call cannot consume the advance silently, never that every licensed re-ask fits.

states.does: Reads the seam once (element_survey), composes Lesson candidates and Journey marks, mints every display_id, validates, writes the survey record to the run workspace.
states.governing: the served-renderings input rule, the candidate model, the display-ID rule

states.owner_supplies: one tag name, or the standing option
states.governing: the post-tag-selection window, the wait rule

states.does: Bounded tag-scoped read; emits the composition pin naming the tag, the survey pin and the member set served per group.

states.input_shape: typed claims record carrying composition_pin and one claim per group

record_example.claims: $per-group:<the GroupClaim for this group, composed from this group's members in `material` -- one sentence, no citation>

states.refusal: claims whose group/member set is not a subset of the composition pin are refused, naming the members outside it

states.input_shape: typed per-group record, judged: true, one entry per composed group, carrying the judge pin; each SubGroup carries a `coherence` label from the closed set tight | related | forced and a `coherence_why` sentence

subgroups.name: <a SubGroup name>
subgroups.claim: <the SubGroupClaim, composed from this SubGroup's members in `material` -- one sentence, no citation>
members: <ids drawn from this group's `members` in `groups[0]`, and from nowhere else>

verdicts.coherence_why: <one sentence: why this SubGroup holds together at that label>

states.refusal: a missing group entry, a bare array, or an absent judge pin is refused; a SubGroup whose `coherence` is outside the closed set, or that carries no `coherence_why`, is refused — the label is the judge's and is never defaulted here; and a judged-EMPTY outcome for a group at or above the split threshold is refused, because at that size WHETHER to split is the engine's decision rather than the judge's (semantic subdivision)
states.governing: semantic subdivision, measurement before offering, the report identity

states.does: Renders the CoTagGroups display: groups by co-tag, mints GroupIDs, renders the composed claims and the SubGroups J2 placed.
states.governing: the display's serve rule, the SubGroup threshold, GroupClaim-first rendering, the emit-time refusal
the post-tag-selection window, the wait rule

states.input_shape: typed array of {claim, strands} objects, exactly `limits.thesis_candidates` of them, each combining 2 to 8 LessonDisplayIDs THIS report renders
states.refusal: a count other than the declared limit, a claim spanning more than one line, a strand list outside 2 to 8, a strand no entered Group or SubGroup carries, and a repeated strand are each refused
states.governing: the Thesis candidates, the neighborhood section's shape
states.ordering: AHEAD OF J3_neighborhood, and that is this row's whole reason for existing at this position (kogaki#861, owner ruling 2026-09-05). The neighborhood judgment names, per candidate, the Thesis candidate it serves; a target can only be refused against a candidate set that already exists, so the ids are FIXED here and J3 reads them. The alternative — one judgment composing candidates and neighborhood together — was declined: the model would supply the list and the targets into it in the same act, and nothing outside that act could refuse a target naming a candidate the same record invented.

states.does: Enumerates the provenance-neighborhood's mechanical candidates for the entered set and writes them to the run workspace, so the judgment point below has something to judge.
states.governing: the settled-strand-set input, the neighborhood section's shape

states.input_shape: typed record keyed by candidate slug, each carrying one free-form claim, one level from the harness-fixed set, and one target naming the Thesis candidate it serves and its role for that candidate
states.refusal: a level outside the closed set, a level with no claim, a judgment with no target, a target that is not a TC id, a target naming a Thesis candidate the thesis_candidates state did not compose, and a key no mechanical candidate carries are each refused, naming the offending slug

states.governing: the Full Report, the report identity, location and naming, the provenance neighborhood

states.owner_supplies: ratification of the trim, or its negation
states.conditional: entered only when a trim is proposed

states.owner_supplies: up to three Strand ids, or free text

states.does: Terminal. The flow ends here; Brief is outside the boundary and this table neither names nor guarantees a Brief launch.

cotag_groups.writer: one private CoTagGroups renderer, called by the writing state the table binds it to
cotag_groups.rule: overwritten on every render; ONE writer, private to the executor (SPEC-terrain, write authority)

full_report.rule: overwritten per pull; identity is the report identity's quadruple (pin, query, judge pin, neighborhood judgment record)

owner_surface_coverage.rule: DENOMINATOR = the states in this file whose `writes` is non-null (every surviving owner surface, since write authority makes a writing state the only thing that may write one). NUMERATOR = those of them whose `grammar_surface` names a surface present in report-format.json's `surfaces`. A removed subcommand contributes to NEITHER term: it is not a surviving surface, so removal moves the denominator and never the numerator.
owner_surface_coverage.recomputed_never_transcribed: `at_this_version` is a convenience for a human reader and carries no authority. On any disagreement the rule above wins and the field is repaired — never the rule to the figure. No registered check executes the rule (SPEC what is not carried).

bound_to_a_state.cotags: the cotag_groups state. CALLABLE for composition, REFUSED at the owner artifact: a standalone invocation whose rendering destination resolves to the repository's `reports/` fails rather than writing CoTagGroups.md (write authority). Redirect it and the composition proceeds — a rendering whose lifetime is the run is not an owner artifact (specs/SPEC.md's lifetime discriminator — lifetime, not format or audience-in-principle).
bound_to_a_state.report: the full_report state. Same write authority as `cotags`: callable for composition, and refused where the destination resolves to the repository's `reports/`, so FullReport.md is written only from the writing state the table binds the renderer to (write authority).
bound_to_a_state.run: THE CONTROL PLANE, bound to the table AS A WHOLE rather than to one state: it reads the run record, executes the states this file declares until the next declared WAIT or the TERMINAL, writes that state's artifact, and stops. RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT UNCOVERED (kogaki#901): the totality below is stated over EVERY dispatcher case, and `run` appeared in none of the five maps before this head — a defect against this file by its own rule. It went unseen because nothing computes the totality: no code in this repository reads these maps, so the invariant is prose and its only reader is a person.
bound_to_a_state.start: the same states `run` executes, entered by the harness's SKILL EXPANSION rather than by a hook event (kogaki#1027). It opens the run, advances to its first wait and stops; it refuses an existing run record, so it never resumes one. It is in THIS map and not in `owner_executed_entry_points` for a reason worth stating: the owner types no command here either — the terrain skill file's one `!` line is executed by the harness at invocation, before the model sees anything — so an entry point nobody types belongs with the states it runs. Its transitions carry the `skill-expansion` executor kind and no hook fields, because no hook event produced them.

non_flow_entry_points.self-test: seam-free identity-cite fixture pass; emits no owner surface, carries no sequencing authority
non_flow_entry_points.validate: runs survey-record validation; emits no owner surface

entry_point_accounting: EVERY case in src/terrain.mjs's dispatcher appears in exactly one of the 5 maps above (bound_to_a_state, removed_entry_points, retired_entry_points, non_flow_entry_points, owner_executed_entry_points), and THAT TOTALITY is the property rather than the count: the next entry point is covered by the totality rather than by having been remembered. A case in none of them, or in two, is a defect against this file. THREE MAPS ARE EMPTY AT THIS HEAD AND ALL THREE KEYS STAY. `owner_executed_entry_points` has been empty since v14 (kogaki#856): the owner types no command in this flow. `removed_entry_points` and `retired_entry_points` are emptied at kogaki#901, propagating SPEC-terrain v36 §"A removed entry point is DELETED, and leaves no stub": the nine refusing stubs are gone from the dispatcher, so there is no case left for either map to account for. The keys stay on the same ground the v14 one did — an empty map states the set is empty, where a deleted key would leave a reader unable to tell an empty set from a map somebody dropped. The totality holds over 8 cases and 2 non-empty maps: survey, cotags, compose-input, report, run and start in bound_to_a_state; self-test and validate in non_flow_entry_points. `start` joined at kogaki#1027, and it is the case that made the executor's TWO invocation acts visible in this map rather than one. `default:` is the unknown-command banner and is not a case. THE TOTALITY IS COMPUTED, and by `checks/check-entry-point-accounting.sh` (kogaki#986) — an editor of these maps is told here that a reader exists, because a reader nothing points at is one the next editor works around. Before that member the sentence above was prose whose only reader was a person who happened to look, and at the head before kogaki#901 it did not hold: `run` was a dispatcher case in none of the five maps, and stood across the #856 and #861 sittings, both of which edited these very maps. The sentence STAYS — the check reads it and refuses if it goes, so the declaration and its instrument retire together or not at all.
